root.name: Zaire Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nc6 2. d5 Nb8 3. e4 Nf6 4. e5 Ng8

overview: Black plays 1...Nc6 2.d5 Nb8 3.e4 Nf6 4.e5 Ng8, shuffling the knights back while White builds a big central pawn wedge. White has gained space and two tempi, and Black has to find a way back with ...e6 or ...d6 and ...Nf6 again. It is a joke-like sideline that gives Black a worse position.

white_ideas.idea: Use the extra space with pawns on d5 and e5
Develop with Nf3, Bd3, and Nc3

black_ideas.idea: Develop and aim for ...Nf6 once the e5 pawn is challenged

typical_structures.structure: White pawns d5 and e5 against Black pawns on a7 to h7

character.notes: A line where Black has lost time and White simply has to develop.

gambit.notes: Material is level; no pawn is given up.

soundness.notes: Black has wasted several tempi and White has an easy edge.

structure.notes: White has an advanced pawn centre.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players.

level.notes: Little theory; a dubious line is not a first repertoire.

character.reason: Neither forcing nor hard to break down; Black is simply worse.

soundness.reason: Black has wasted time and handed White a free centre.

structure.reason: White pawns on d5 and e5 cramp Black.

plans.reason: White has space from the advanced pawns.
